summary.text: Patient A is a 11-year-old male with beta-thalassemia major and transfusion-dependent thalassemia, with a peak ferritin of 7,077 ng/mL and T2-weighted MRI suggestive of iron deposition.

Between 2019 and 2021 he was transitioned from chronic simple RBC transfusions to RBCX after developing iron overload with deferasirox use; Table 2 gives simple transfusion interval 2 weeks versus RBCX interval 4 weeks, mean ferritin 6,530 before and 1,382 after, and blood utilization 4,200 mL before and 5,625 mL after.

summary.text: Patient C is a 14-year-old male with beta-thalassemia/HbE and transfusion-dependent thalassemia, with a peak ferritin of 1,400 ng/mL, nephrotoxicity complicating deferasirox management.

article_limitations: Retrospective case series of five patients labelled A to E; individual-level data come from one descriptive paragraph, Table 2, a dose paragraph, and Figure 1. No narrative case descriptions, dates, or individual adverse events.

Cohort statements (188 procedures; 17 vasovagal reactions, 8 asymptomatic hypotensive reactions, 4 citrate toxicity reactions; median ferritin and P value; 4,085 mL average extra blood use; averages of 3.2 and 5 weeks) are not copied to individuals.

RBCX settings (pre-transfusion hematocrit target 29% or higher, post-transfusion hematocrit target 37-38%, FCR 30%, isovolemic hemodilution omitted, transfused unit hematocrit assumed 60%, Rh and Kell matched donor blood, Terumo Spectra Optia system) are series-level protocol statements with no per-patient schema field and are not recorded as facts.

Table 2 prints no unit for ferritin and no averaging window for blood utilization (the text elsewhere uses ng/mL and a 3-month comparison); neither was borrowed. Difference column equals pre minus post for every row.

The lead phrase "At the time of RBCX initiation" is applied only to patient A's age; peak ferritin has no printed time. The RBCX transition window (2019 to 2021) is stated for the five patients as a group.
Figure 1 values are plot estimates, not printed values.

Deferasirox dose changes for patients D and E are recorded as the two stated doses each (before and after the increase) with no printed times. Patient C's chelation stop is "by the 2-year time point" with no stated anchor.
Figure 1 plot estimates for patient D reach about 3,200 ng/mL at 3 months pre, slightly above the stated peak of 3,060 ng/mL; within plot-estimate uncertainty, not treated as a conflict.
